paragraphs.text: Welcome back to another episode of Tis the Podcast, the podcast that's determined to keep the Christmas spirit alive all year round, including the month of July, which we're officially in. I am Anthony. I'm Julia. I'm Thom. Can y'all believe it is July? It feels like July outside. I mean, heat-wise, I can believe it. But time-wise, doesn't this year seem like it's going quick? It is insane.
It's insane. Insane. Joann has put out all their Halloween stuff.
Not locally.
Yeah. So, okay, have you been to Joann's today? There are Joann's stores near me.
I said, have you been today?
No.

They just put it all out. But let me tell you, just before recording, I saw the new Indiana Jones movie. And while I was at the mall, I walked into Bath & Body Works, and I went up to the sales associate near the front of the store, who was young, in her 20s or early 30s, whatever, and I was like, "Look, it's going to be a weird question, but when are you putting out the fall stuff?" And she looked at me like I had 20 heads. She was like, "Sir, it is still June." And I was like, "Yes, but in the past y'all always put it out right after the Fourth of July, so I was wondering if you had a date." And she said, "I have no clue."
She don't know. She don't know.

So Hannah works at Bath & Body Works also, but she's on a resetting crew, so she does these periodic Sunday nights where they reset the store. Well, she's got one coming up Sunday, and you'd better believe I'm going to be asking her what's up.
Quick question for you, Julia.
Yeah?
Does she get a store discount?
I think she still gets a discount.
Does Hannah love her avuncular Uncle Anthony, who gives her access to all the TV shows?
She does.
Tell Hannah I may be reaching out to her on Instagram.
I'm pretty sure she gets the discount. It's funny, I haven't asked yet. If she's part-time, it's 30%. But I may have a bigger coupon for you, Anthony.
Even better. You've got the inside track.
No, I just have a bunch of coupons. But yeah, I saw Indiana Jones tonight, and it was fine. It was fun. It was fine. I mean, it wasn't the best thing ever, but it wasn't Crystal Skull.
I mean, they get progressively… it doesn't look that good.
Phoebe Waller-Bridge. I'll tell you this: Phoebe Waller-Bridge, who's the British girl in it, she stars in Fleabag on Amazon. She would make an excellent Selina Kyle in James Gunn's DC Universe.
Okay. I love her.
She gave me all the Catwoman vibes in this movie. And speaking of the DC Universe, we have our new Superman and Lois Lane.
We do? Were they officially cast? Because I've seen two different articles, and they're both different.
They were officially cast. James Gunn confirmed it. David Corenswet is going to be playing Clark Kent slash Superman.
So much better than our other option.

He was in The Politician on Netflix, and House of Cards. He was in the fantastic horror movie Pearl, which is a prequel to X. He was in some HBO miniseries. He's great. And he actually looks like a little-younger Henry Cavill as well.
He really does. Although, did you see the thing Jerry posted?
Oh yeah, about how he looks like the cheap version of Henry Cavill. Froot Loops, and then Henry was below it, and then they had off-brand, store-bought stuff, and they had David below that.
He's just younger and smaller. I don't think it's a bad cast. They were going to go with... Who were they? The rumor was it was going to be what's-his-face.
Nicholas Hoult.
He got passed up for Batman. He got passed up for Superman now. Supposedly he's up for Lex Luthor as well.
Okay. He could be Lex Luthor. Valid.
He's too small-framed.

We'll get back to Lex Luthor in a minute, because there are rumors about who else is up for that role, who I like better. But Lois Lane is going to be played by Rachel Brosnahan, who was my first choice. The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel. She has the potential to be the best Lois Lane ever. She exudes that energy. So this is the first Jewish Superman and Lois.
Is he Jewish too?
He is. I think so. But it's fun to me, because people online are more excited about her casting than his, because he's a little more unknown. People are very excited she got Lois Lane.
Yeah, it's a great choice.

I think it's an amazing choice. She is a very powerful actress. Now, supposedly Nicholas Hoult is up for Lex Luthor, but supposedly so are Alexander Skarsgård and Bill Skarsgård. They're both up for it.
I'm tired of the Skarsgård brothers, y'all. Let's give somebody else a chance.

Well, I'll tell you, both are fantastic actors. I'd be fine with either of them. But in my dream scenario, if I was James Gunn, I'd make Alexander Skarsgård Lex Luthor, and Bill Skarsgård the Joker in the new Batman movie, and then you have both brothers playing supervillains. That's what I would do.
Okay. That is a family full of villains. Although Stellan, the older he gets, the more you're like, well, you're so precious and old, and you're so cute.
Supposedly Alexander Skarsgård is not in the top running anymore.
Well, Bill Skarsgård I'm fine with. Bill is Pennywise, so I've always pictured him as the Joker, for obvious reasons.
Which Lex Luthors have you liked in the past, Anthony?
Gene Hackman. But Jon Cryer has been the best Lex Luthor.
Jon Cryer? When was he Lex Luthor?
He's in Supergirl, on TV.
Okay.
Yeah. Bald. And Abraham from The Walking Dead is Lex Luthor currently on Superman & Lois, on TV, and he's pretty good.
I'll bet he is.
I did not buy Jesse Eisenberg as Lex Luthor.
He tried to do the whole tech bro Lex Luthor. That's not Lex Luthor.
What about Kevin Spacey? Where does he rate? I kind of liked him as Lex Luthor.
Jesse Eisenberg was just playing… he was still just playing Mark Zuckerberg.

Yeah, he was. Now, on my other podcast, you know, DC Unlimited, shameless plug, we're going to be recording next week about the casting news, asking people who they would want to see as Jor-El and Ma and Pa Kent. So I'm going to throw that to both of you. Who would you like to see in this rebooted version as Superman's adoptive parents and birth father?
Diane Lane as Ma Kent was perfect, and nobody else will be Ma Kent. She was perfect. And I liked Kevin Costner's Pa Kent, too.
I'd kind of like to see Henry Cavill playing Jor-El. I think it'd be a fun way to keep that moving, you know?
So for Jor-El, I kind of want Matthew McConaughey.
Alright, alright, alright.

Because Jor-El's supposed to be younger anyway. They age differently. You need somebody, a good actor, with gravitas. And I would say Christian Bale, but he already played Batman, and he was in a Thor movie. He's not going to do Superman. But I could see Matthew McConaughey. And for my Pa Kent, I want Laura Linney for Ma Kent and Steve Carell as Pa Kent. Silver-fox Steve Carell. Serious dramatic actor Steve Carell. I think he could pull it off nowadays. The guy has range. And then Perry White: I'm convinced James Gunn's going to cast Michael Rooker, because he casts Michael Rooker in everything. He's the newspaper editor at the Daily Planet. The boss.
Gotcha.
And Jimmy Olsen: the guy from Abbott Elementary. Jacob as Jimmy.
Oh my gosh, he would be perfect. The geeky photographer, fanboying over Superman.
That's funny. That would be funny.
So that's my cast. So listeners, if you're DC fans, let me know who you would cast.
I haven't given it a lot of thought, but I think Bryan Cranston would be a fun Pa Kent.
All Bryan Cranston. I kind of want Bryan Cranston as Commissioner Gordon. Or Lex Luthor.
Oh, man. So, 4th of July is coming up, y'all. Do you guys have any plans?

How are you celebrating America's birthday? Ed, you should celebrate it, because we may only have democracy for another year. Wait! If we have Henry Cavill playing... No, we need somebody playing Pa Kent to be a good guy. I was going to say Dean Cain.
I don't mind getting one of the older... If Christopher Reeve is still alive, you would have to get Christopher Reeve to play Jor-El.
We are celebrating the birth of my wife for July 4th. Oh yeah, I forgot that was her birthday too. What are you guys doing for it?
I don't know. She hasn't decided yet.
What are you doing for the Fourth, Julia? What are you and the family doing? How are you celebrating America's birthday?

I don't know yet. I was supposed to check today if there were any plans being made and I was included in them, which is usually what happens, because being centrally located typically means people gravitate toward your location, and I find out about it with very little time to prepare. So, TBD. I did order two cobblers from my favorite bakery in Tulsa, Antoinette, that I'm so excited about, because I love me some cobbler. And that's really all I care about at this moment: I'm not working that day, and I'm going to have cobbler in my face. Super excited. And hopefully our neighbors will have spent all the money they usually spend on fireworks and illegally set them off behind our house on the golf course.
I've just been thinking and looking at actors.
Jeff Bridges and Elisabeth Shue for Jonathan and Martha Kent.
She is that age now. It's hard to believe.
I like Elisabeth Shue.
I do too. I like Jeff Bridges too, but…
I always wanted Elisabeth Shue to be my babysitter.
Me too.
Ever since Adventures in Babysitting?
Uh-huh. She can still babysit me. I'm okay with that.
Pervert.
Well, it's been a while since I called you a pervert on air. I feel bad.
It has been. I know. I'm looking forward to you doing that in person.
I can't hear you say that in person. I have no plans for the Fourth, and it's glorious.
No-plan holidays are the best.
It's not even a real holiday.
Oh, stop. It is a real holiday.
Yeah, congratulations. We took America from the people who were already here, and we're celebrating that. But if it's nice, I'm just planning to lie by the pool and read. That's all I need.
This one's celebrating fighting the British.
The British are the ones who took it away.
From the British. That's true.
So we're the good British ancestors.
Well, no. Our British ancestors still suck too.
Whatever. We're the less evil British ancestors.
You know about Andrew Jackson, right?

Oh, I do. Yeah, we're not the good ones. An odd choice for the former president to have his picture hanging in the Oval Office. I mean, par for the course, but still an odd choice for any president to put that picture in the Oval Office.
Oh, man. Fourth of July, which means Christmas in July is coming up, and I have an idea for what we should do for that.

Actually, Matt Yurick gave us this idea or a good friend, Matt Yurick gave us this idea on Facebook a few weeks ago. He thinks we should do a script reading of elf or another Christmas movie, cast it with a bunch of our friends and us and record an episode. And I think that'd be a fun thing to do. That'd be fun.
And it's very clear who each of us would play.

Who would I play? buddy julie would be jovie and i'd be walter i mean come on right i think you should be mr greenville the question is do we cast santa matt as santa because he does not like ed asner's santa well we give him an opportunity to put his spin on santa yeah that's true we don't need to do it exactly. We should be Peter Dinklage. No, Ron's gotta be Peter Dinklage. Oh my gosh.
But I think this is what we should do. We should try to coordinate that. I can't believe it's July.
I can't believe it's July either. And I can't believe one of us has to coordinate that.
I would ask which of us is the boss here, to coordinate that, but I think we all know the answer.
I'll do it.
It's the New Yorker, for sure. And that was my awkward segue into what we're covering tonight.
It worked, it worked.
Tonight, we're covering the '80s sitcom Who's the Boss?
[Sings the theme song, "Brand New Life."]

Now for those who don't know, Who's the Boss is about a widower and former pro baseball player, Tony Micelli, who takes a job as the housekeeper for a high-powered divorce businesswoman, Angela Bauer, and her son. He and his daughter, Samantha, move into the Bauer residence where Tony's laid-back personality conflicts with Angela's type A behavior.
So, histories with Who's the Boss? Julia.

I think I would catch this probably on Nick at Nite, because I asked my parents if they watched it, and my dad said no, and Mom said, "I think so," which probably means no. So I think I've caught episodes here and there, just in reruns and syndication, and it was never a staple in our house, though I'm familiar with the storyline. And it was a blast of nostalgia watching it, not for the show itself but for the era it was set in, which was fun.
And it's fine. I did watch this as a kid. My family watched it, and it was fine. There was some acting that was not as good as I remembered as a kid.
But, you know, it was fun to watch. It felt nostalgic. I liked one of the episodes a lot more than the other.
Me too. Yeah, I watched this all the time growing up, between Nick at Night and ABC Family used to show a lot of these shows, like in the mid-afternoon, like right after school.

And Who's the Boss? for a while. It got a lot of airtime, so I think I've seen most of the show. But yeah, I always liked it. I always liked the fun concept: the male housekeeper moving in with the female boss.
Yeah. Plus Alyssa Milano, who… I mean, I was a young boy in the '90s. Of course I had a crush on Alyssa Milano, and it's fun seeing her beginnings here.

Marty mentioned that. When he asked what we were covering, he was like, "Oh, I had such a crush on her growing up." And I was like, "Who, Judith Light?" No idea why. Probably because if I had watched this, I would have had a crush on Tony Danza, right? So, massive age separation. But he was like, "Alyssa Milano, obviously." And I'm like, yeah, that probably makes more sense. But he first fell in love with her in Commando. She was the kid in Commando, right?
One of those, yeah. Arnold, whichever one it was.
So that's where he first saw Alyssa Milano. I'm like, that makes sense.

I fell in love with her here, and then I started watching Charmed, where she was one of the witch sisters, and she was the fun-loving, more quote-unquote wild of the three, and I really fell in love with her there, during my preteen years. But yeah, I liked it, and revisiting these episodes today was a blast from the past. It was a hit of nostalgia. It was definitely more over the top than I remembered, the acting specifically, especially Tony Danza. But I didn't hate my time watching it or anything. It was fine.
So let's run through the cast. Tony Micelli is played by Tony Danza. "Hold me closer, Tony Danza," as Phoebe Buffay would sing.
He got his start on Taxi and then moved to Who's the Boss, for which he was nominated for Emmys and Four Golden Globes.
Really?
In 98, Tony Danza won the People's Choice Award for Favorite Male Performer in his sitcom, The Tony Danza Show.
He had a show?

He had a show. Not to be confused with his daytime variety talk show in the early 2000s called The Tony Danza Show. And he has also starred in films such as Hollywood Knights, Going Ape!, Angels in the Outfield, Crash, and Don Jon.
I loved him in Angels in the Outfield.

Me too. I loved everything in Angels in the Outfield. I like him in general. He seems like a decent enough human being, from everything I've seen of him. Plus, you know, typical Italian New Yorker. I feel a kindred bond with this guy.
Sure. I know Thom is grateful to him for a plethora of Family Guy jokes on his behalf.

They had some good Family Guy episodes and references to this, including an episode where they did a drawing for what the neighborhood parade was going to be themed, and I remember this is from season one, Peter put in there the Who's the Boss? episode when Tony walked in on Angela in the shower. All the floats were themed to that, and one of them is like, "Oh, this one's a miss. That's not Angela, that is Mona." But I like the way they used tree bark on her back to show age spots. And that is also a classic episode of Who's the Boss?
When he walked in on her in the shower? That's one of the first episodes.
Yeah.
Oh, wow. Just like one of the first episodes of The Nanny was her walking in on him in the shower too.

So Judith Light plays Angela Bower, his boss slash love interest as the series goes on. She made her Broadway debut in A Doll's House. Her breakthrough role was in the ABC soap opera One Life to Live. She starred in Who's the Boss? She's starred in Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. She starred in Ugly Betty. She starred in the remake of Dallas. She starred in Transparent, for Amazon, for which she received several Golden Globe, Primetime Emmy, and Critics' Choice Award nominations. She starred in American Crime Story: The Assassination of Gianni Versace.
And only a few years ago, she was awarded a star in the Hollywood Rock of Fame.
Golly, only in the last few years?
So I like her. I liked a lot of her recent work, like American Crime Story and Transparent. She definitely grew out of the soap opera, over-the-top broad comedy she did earlier in her career.
Alyssa Milano, Be Still My Heart, plays Samantha Maselli, Tony's teenage daughter or preteen daughter. I don't even know at this age, probably preteen.
Be still my heart. Preteen me.

You know what I meant. For the actress now. So she got her start on TV in Who's the Boss? She played Jennifer Mancini in Melrose Place, Phoebe Halliwell in Charmed, Billie Cunningham in My Name Is Earl, Savannah in Mistresses. She played Renata Murphy in Wet Hot American Summer: Ten Years Later, and Coraline Armstrong in Insatiable. And nowadays she spends a lot of her time as a political activist.
Did everybody that was on Charmed turn into that role? A political activist? Isn't Rose McGowan a political activist?
I mean, yeah. She does climate change and women's rights.
I think she was kind of forced into it with the #MeToo movement. Not unwittingly, but it took coaxing to get her to come forward about the Harvey Weinstein stuff, right?
Wait, do I have the wrong show? No, Charmed was the one with the witches. Was Shannen Doherty always a witch?
She was the original one. Then, when she got killed off, they brought in Paige as their half-sister.
Gotcha. Okay. I was looking at the cover, and I'm like, maybe I have the wrong three-sister witch show.

"The power of three will set us free." That's what they always said. I mean, we talked enough about Alyssa Milano in the opening here, but we all knew her. Danny Pintauro plays Jonathan Bower, Angela's son, who had very, very little to do in these two episodes. If he had three lines between these two episodes, that's a lot. He starred in Who's the Boss?, obviously, and the 1983 horror film Cujo.
Oh, he was the kid?

Oh my gosh. This guy's had a rough life. In '97, the National Enquirer tabloid outed him as gay. In 2015, he revealed he was HIV-positive, which he'd contracted back in 2003, and he had been addicted to meth. So he was sadly one of those child stars who had a lot of issues later in life. He hasn't been in much in recent years. He played himself in the child stars edition of The Weakest Link back in 2001. He had a guest role in The Secret Life of the American Teenager. He was himself on Oprah: Where Are They Now? back in 2015. Last year, though, he was in A Country Christmas Harmony, as a character named Eugene, so you may see him one of these days.

And now, my favorite character in this show by far, I don't know how y'all feel about it, is Mona Robinson, Angela's mother, as portrayed by Katherine Helmond, who we did cover before. She plays Debra's mom on Everybody Loves Raymond, and she was in those Christmas episodes.
Oh, we sure did.
But I love Katherine Helmond in everything. This show, Coach, Everybody Loves Raymond. She was in Family Plot, from Alfred Hitchcock. She was in Garry Marshall's Overboard. She's fantastic.
Love that movie so much. Overboard, one of my favorite movies from the '80s.

And we sadly lost her back in 2019. But she's fantastic, and I loved her role on the show too, the sassy mom to uptight Angela. And she was always an ardent supporter of Tony, from the very beginning.
We saw that in the first episode we covered tonight.
So let's jump right in. The first episode we are covering is called "The Christmas Card." This aired during season three, on December 16th, 1986, and it was the 11th episode of that season.
Well, first of all, we have a guest star in this episode we've covered before: Kalabar, from Halloweentown. Our villain from Halloweentown plays Angela's serious boyfriend in this episode.
Our villain of this episode.
Okay, I needed some background on this. I was like, why does Tony Danza hate him so much, whatever his name is? Okay, so she and Geoffrey are dating?
Yep.
And has he been around for quite some time?
I would assume so, because they get engaged at some point, from what I was reading. But I do not remember him at all.
Okay. All right, thank you.
But Angela was seeking other suitors, because she and Tony had the will-they-won't-they thing happening.
Will they won't they, of course.

So the family's getting ready for Christmas. Angela is dating Jeffrey, who's this richy rich gentleman who... And nobody likes him, right? Nobody likes him. Tony doesn't. Mom. Mona doesn't. but Angela is totally enamored by him and she's actually going to be spending Christmas with his family
Tony and his daughter and Mona aren't invited. Apparently his mom's already hired the help.

Yeah, because Angela suggests, "Oh, why don't you bring your family here, and we can have it here," because Tony makes a big ham and a big old Christmas dinner at home. And he's like, "Mom's already hired the caterers." She says "the help."
The help.

Because Tony's like, "Oh yes, the help." You see this inner conflict, where he sees himself as part of the family, but because he's not included, his daughter's not included, and Angela's mother, for whatever reason, is not included, he feels not part of the family.
Did I miss a line of dialogue? Was Mona included, and she just decided not to go? Because Mona's like, "Oh, I'm going to stay here and have goose with Tony and Sam," which I loved.
I don't remember if she was explicitly invited or not. It was weird.

Yeah. Are we supposed to get the sense that Richie Rich Geoffrey is… that the kids are thinking, if he marries my mom, they're going to ship me off to boarding school? Is he that kind of unlikable, where you're almost like, we hate this guy so much, how would Angela ever have been interested? You know how they'll do that in sitcoms, and you're like, that person would never go for that person?
Yeah. I don't think he's like that.
No, I don't either. It's more that he's just not Tony. You want her to be with Tony.
And by the way, I hate that trope so much in sitcoms and movies, and that's why I loved, in Mrs. Doubtfire, how Pierce Brosnan was legit in love with those kids and Sally Field.
Yeah. And he's a good guy.
Yeah. Movie trivia for you: that was not the original script. In the original script, he was not going to be a good guy, but they decided to make him a good guy to change it up and be different.
Such a good change.
Yep. That's such a good change. So Geoffrey is clearly, because of his money, going to do something big for Angela for Christmas.

Well, he reveals to Tony his gift for Angela is right here, and he pats his pocket. And for a second I thought, oh, he's going to propose to her. But no, it just turns out to be earrings. Very expensive earrings.
Which makes Tony… yep.
I thought, at the moment when Tony's worried about money, oh, we're going to have a Gift of the Magi situation here.
Uh-huh. Quasi-Magi, for sure.
Yeah, it was quasi, but I was expecting it to be full-blown Magi somewhere.
And Tony is intimidated because he wants to get Angela something special. And he was knitting her something, which turned out to look awful. He didn't know how to knit.

And he feels intimidated by Geoffrey's money. So earlier in this episode, Mr. Ferguson, who I guess is a neighbor or something, wants Tony's baseball card. Tony was a former professional baseball player, so he had a few baseball cards. And Tony said he only had one, and he gave it away to a man in the hospital who was dying, and the family ended up selling it so they could go to Paris. Then we find out this is a lie. Tony just has it upstairs. He wants to keep it in the family, so he can show the kids one day. He doesn't want Richie Rich to buy it.

And I like the scene afterward, where Sam's like, "You didn't sell your card?" And he's like, "No, I didn't. None of that story was real." And she's like, "Okay, well, next time you tell it, ditch Paris and have the guy die." And they decide that in the next telling, he should be buried with Tony's baseball card.

Right away, you can already tell where this is going. He's going to end up selling the baseball card. But we're not there yet, because while Tony has this dilemma, Angela has a dilemma of her own. And what is that, Julia?
Angela's dilemma: she can't find the perfect gift for Tony. I keep wanting to call him Tony Danza, but it's Tony in the show and Tony in real life, so his name is still Tony.
Okay. You're good. Just go with the first name.

Let's just leave it at that. Yeah. She can't find the perfect thing for him. What do you get the guy who has everything? And she cares for him. You get that sense that she cares for him. She wants it to be special.

Well, I like that conversation she has with Mona. She's like, "What do you get him? Because we're kind of this, but not kind of that." And she goes on for a good 30 seconds trying to describe the relationship, and Mona's like, "Why don't you go to the store and tell them you're looking for a gift to sum that up?"

I do like when they come home from the store. Mona goes shopping with her, and Mona was very thoughtful. She got her own gift so that Angela wouldn't have to worry about it. "How did you get your own gift, Mother?" "Oh, I just put it on your charge card. You were really generous. You really shouldn't have done something so extravagant." "Well, I want it to be a surprise." "I love it so much."

But of course, Angela heard Tony tell Mr. Ferguson the story about his baseball card, so she's like, I will purchase his baseball card back. So she goes to a collector's shop with Mona and tries haggling. Well, the guy haggles with her, and Mona's like…
She's eager.
Yeah, she's eager. And Mona tries to pull her back, but she ends up paying, what, 150, 200 bucks for the card?
Two-hundred-something for it.
250. 250 was the figure.

So, interesting question, Tony. Like 200, right? Because he doesn't have the card in his possession. Do pawn shops do that, like, I'll go find this thing? I thought you just walk in, you see something you want, you buy it.
Oh, well, he's a collector. A memorabilia collector.
I don't know that they would set a price before knowing how they'd get hold of it, though. It seems risky.
Right. It seems very risky.
Okay. I thought it was a pawn shop, sorry.

But she was desperate. She was like, "Oh, yeah, it's a Christmas gift." "Oh, you need it for Christmas?" And I love Mona, the whole time, is doing it right, because she ends up purchasing, I forget what…
A poster.
A poster. And the guy's like, "Twenty bucks." And she's like, "It's very rare." "Very rare. It's 25." And she's like, "I'll give you five." And he's like, "Done."
I don't want to be a pedant, but she did say six. It was six dollars.
Every time Thom starts out with "I don't want to be a pedant," listeners, he's going to be.

I don't know. I remember everything about both of these episodes, and that's not usually the case, and I watched them several days ago, but I remember every detail about this for some reason. Of course, Christmas morning comes.
Geoffrey got Tony a robot, a little robot to help with the chores around the house.
So cute.
It is really cute. It's every '90s sitcom robot you've ever seen.
It looks so much like ALF.

What happens Christmas morning: Sam goes to give Angela the Tiffany's box from Richie Rich, and Tony's like, "No, that's actually from me." She opens it, and it's a Tiffany vase, for some reason. Which is funny, because in The Nanny, Mr. Sheffield's hot friend gets a vase for Christmas, too.
Vases being a big deal. Crystal in general was a big dang deal.
It does not hold water.
I mean, it does hold water, but the idea of getting a vase does not hold water nowadays. But yes, he gets a vase. Somebody says "a vase," and he goes, "It's a vahz."
You can find those things all day long at estate sales now, for next to nothing.
And Angela gives Tony his baseball card, and Tony's over the moon. "This looks just like my baseball card. This looks like the one I sold. Even with the little bend in the corner."
This is my card. And he realizes what she did, and then she realizes what he did. And they have this very sweet, unspoken moment.
That Jeffrey finally interrupts like, should we go to my parents' house?

"I've got to get her out of here. They're about to make out." They leave. And then we get the little scene that plays with the credits. Later that night, the kids are in bed, Tony's in the kitchen. Angela didn't like any of the food. It wasn't good. So Tony heats her up his Christmas everything, and he's so excited, too.
This is my favorite scene in the whole episode.
I like this one 100%.
Yeah. He's so proud of this turkey and all this, and she's even like, "Is there any cranberry sauce?" And he had it on the counter. And that's a running thing throughout the show: he's a good cook.
Italians, of course.
Yeah. And she's so excited, because he's going to sit and eat with her too.
So he serves himself some as well.
Yep. Even though he pulls the "I'm so full," but then he ends up having some. It's Christmas.
It also reminded me of Friends.
